expectations.text: Opens with a hook rather than throat-clearing
expectations.evidence: "I've counted it now. Roughly ten times this year, I've committed to waking up early to pray and journal before work."

expectations.text: Contains at least one question-style H2 header
expectations.evidence: The post has no H2 headers at all -- a single title followed by continuous prose.

expectations.text: Uses short paragraphs including at least one single-line paragraph
expectations.evidence: Every paragraph runs 5-9 dense sentences; no single-line paragraphs anywhere.

expectations.text: Does not fabricate a tidy resolution
expectations.evidence: "I don't have this fixed... So this isn't a post about how I solved it."

expectations.text: Ending is a genuine reflective landing tied to material already in the post, not a generic motivational wrap-up
expectations.evidence: Ends on a generic 'isn't X, it's Y' binary-contrast construction ('this isn't a post about how I solved it, it's a post about finally seeing the shape') rather than a callback to a specific concrete image.

expectations.text: Does not contain banned buzzwords or importance-puffery phrases
Uses concrete specifics given in the prompt rather than vague paraphrases
expectations.evidence: 'Roughly ten times' and 'four days' used directly.

claims.claim: Post uses an extended 'monument' metaphor as its central device
claims.evidence: Paragraph 5 builds an entire metaphor ('a monument to how I felt at the retreat... monuments don't need maintenance the way habits do') that is well-written but is a newly invented metaphor rather than a callback, and reads as more essayistic than Asher's typical shorter, punchier landings.

eval_feedback.overall: Structurally the biggest gap is the complete absence of section breaks -- baseline treats this as a single flowing essay where Asher's real posts consistently chunk into question-headed sections.
